title: AcmeMedia integration scratchpad
body:
Call notes (2026-03-01) - quick scratchpad

Attendees: Aisha (Redwood CS), Tom (Redwood solutions), Leah (Redwood AM), Claire Miller (AcmeMedia, Head of Product), Raj Patel (AcmeMedia, Eng lead)

Summary: exploratory tech + procurement call. AcmeMedia wants to embed LLM features into their editorial search and content tagging pipelines. Primary ask is relevance-first semantic search + light summarization for editorial briefs. They are risk-conscious (user PII) and run on AWS only; interested in Private deployment or Dedicated with VPC peering. Budget unclear but pilot must be low-cost (they expect < $5k/mo for the PoC). Timeline: pilot in 6 weeks, production decision in Q3.

Requirements and constraints (as stated by Acme):
- Workloads: batch indexing job (nightly) + near-real-time enrichment on publish (burst traffic).
- Throughput targets: indexing 100k docs/night (avg 3k tokens/doc) and 150 req/s for enrichment at peak (short payloads ~150 tokens).
- Latency SLO: enrichment p95 < 300ms end-to-end if possible. For search, 500ms acceptable for initial rollout.
- Data sensitivity: some articles include user-submitted PII. They need encryption at rest + KMS integration and audit logs.
- Networking: must be able to deploy into their VPC or use a Dedicated instance with private endpoints.
- Model behavior: prefer open-model stack (cost reasons) but will consider Redwood-managed model variants if quality needed.
- Feature needs: embeddings for semantic search, canonicalization/deduping, short abstractive summaries, content tagging (multi-label), and fallback to keyword search when similarity score low.

Technical gotchas / open / flagged items:
- Chunking strategy for large articles: they have 30–40% long-form pieces (20k+ tokens). Need guidance on chunk size + vector index strategy (hybrid indexing?).
- Embedding consistency: want retraining/re-embedding story for model upgrades — how we support reindexing with minimal downtime/cost.
- Cold-cache latency during publish bursts; autoscaling policy needs to be balanced with cost.
- PII filtering: they asked about our recommended approach (pre-filtering vs model-internal redaction). Need concrete doc.
- Streaming: they do not require streaming for enrichments, but editors want fast partial previews while indexing runs. Could propose a small preview API (pull first N tokens).
- Fallback policies: if primary model overloaded, what model variants we can failover to that maintain embedding compatibility? (questions about vector space alignment between variants).

Action items / next steps (assigned):
- Send concise tech spec (2 pager) covering architecture options: Redwood Private (on VPC), Dedicated w/ VPC peering, Hosted with strict privacy controls — include pros/cons, rough cost ballpark for pilot. (Aisha) — due 2026-03-04
- Prepare demo script and notebook: ingest 5 sample articles, show embedding + semantic search + short summaries; include metrics for latency and cost-per-doc. (Tom + Leah) — due 2026-03-11
- Draft recommended chunking strategy + embedding model options + reindex playbook doc. (Solutions eng template exists; adapt). (Tom) — due 2026-03-07
- Security checklist for PII handling (KMS, logs, isolation options) and short Q&A for their legal team. (Leah) — due 2026-03-05
- Create trial account / sandbox with 30-day credits and invite Claire + Raj. Confirm access method (private console vs delegated login). (Aisha) — due 2026-03-03

Questions to clarify on next call (for Claire/Raj):
- Concrete budget for pilot (confirm $/mo ceiling).
- Can they provide representative sample docs (anonymized) for demo? Prefer 50–200 articles across short/long.
- Which AWS region do they require? (critical for Dedicated placement)
- Any compliance constraints beyond standard SOC2/GDPR? (e.g., HIPAA)

Notes to self / quick reminders:
- When drafting cost ballpark, show token/embedding unit math and include Dedicated reserved capacity option (monthly commit) vs usage-hosted tradeoffs.
- Emphasize reindex-cost mitigation: incremental embedding + metadata versioning to avoid full reembed when model minor changes.
- Prepare two fallback model suggestions: 1) same-architecture lower-capacity quantized variant (embedding-compatible); 2) different-architecture fallback with cross-embedding alignment caveats.

Rough architecture sketches (informal):
- Option A: Redwood Private in Acme VPC (best for compliance). Nightly batch jobs push embeddings to their ES/FAISS inside VPC. Enrichment calls routed to local Dedicated pool.
- Option B: Dedicated with VPC peering + private endpoints. Redwood manages runtime, but data stays in peered network. Cheaper ops than full private.
- Option C: Hosted API with strict contracts (no model retention), recommended only if they relax VPC requirement. Fast ramp, cheaper upfront, but less isolated.

Risks / blockers to surface in proposal:
- Cost escalation on reindexing large corpora if model changes frequently. Suggest reindex cadence and monitoring.
- Vector compatibility across model variants is not solved; need to document fallback degradation characteristics.
- Legal sign-off timeline may push pilot start out; include contingency in timeline.

Final note: keep next call focused — demo + short tech spec + clarify pilot budget/regions. Try to lock down sample data within 1 week.

---

Version history / micro-edits:
- 2026-03-01: initial notes from call (this file)
- 2026-03-03: updated with sandbox invite action (Leah)
- 2026-03-05: added chunking + reindex playbook owner
